item.title: #HighlyRecommended : Sisa, a fictional movie about the end stages of the Filipino American war 1898-1902 where over 200,000 people died (and Mark Twain was against). Gut wrenching like America is Not the Heart and Filipiñana. This is what art does: it shines the light on humanity's best and worst.
item.description:
• Draft created: Nov 15, 2026 15:13 (UTC).
  • There is a straight line from the 1898 Filipino American war (Sisa) to Marcos’s brutal dictatorship (America is not the heart) to 2026 (Filipiñana). There are in fact many such lines. We just have to keep drawing them :-)
  • The American men are caricatures but I don’t think that’s bad thing if you think about it from the perspectives of the Filipinos after years of war. All you can see is the other side’s atrocities and stereotypes and in reality, it’s much more nuanced than that. I think everybody can agree though that this was a brutal, barbaric, unnecessary war that was the inevitable consequence of Spanish and American colonialism.
  • The Filipino women particularly, Hilda Koronel’s character, are real people with real PTSD from years of war.
  • Not a hidden war but definitely not something discussed in the Filipino diaspora community. See the links in the next section.
  • Wikipedia: Sisa, Hilda Koronel, there is no wiki page or website that will persist long-term for America is Not the Heart (America is Not the Heart on libby, America is Not the Heart on penguin random house) so check out the author, Elaine Castillo

  • Previously

  • September 19, 2026: Filipiñana 2nd viewing: shot in square i.e. 1:1 re-elect Dr. Palanca, colonialism is not over in the Philippines. This movie still highly recommended.
  • September 7, 2026: HIGHLY RECOMMENDED: Filipiñana, the full 2026 movie, is full arthouse at its most thought (or sleep) provoking and very gut wrenching simultaneously. What actually happened? Did the Doctor and all the Ilustrados get their just desserts :-) ?!?!? Probably not because corruption
  • July 20, 2026: The Americans killed thousands (if not tens of thousands or 100,000 or more) Filipinos in this war and Americans have forgotten about it even though it’s not a hidden conspiracy theory. See Karnow’s In our Image for a biased American history of this ; Mmina Maclang Tamayo aka @thoughtspresso:: It doesn’t escape me as someone from a former US colony (and in many ways continue to be under Uncle Sam’s thumb), that they indeed brought a gift horse to our shores. In the late 1890s, under the guise of friendship, the US staged the Battle of Manila to pretend to help fight off the Spanish colonizers. Then they turned around and became our colonizer
  • September 1, 2019: 28 second :-) podcast: America Is Not The Heart - Elaine Castillo - Highly Recommended!

item.title: ME:: It's hilarious that asking LLMs to do TDD resulted in worse tests than just letting it write tests; Dan Luu:: Test and verification technique effectiveness with Astra
item.description:
Discovered: Nov 12, 2026 15:31 (UTC) ME:: It’s hilarious that asking LLMs to do TDD resulted in worse tests than just letting it write tests; Dan Luu:: Test and verification technique effectiveness with Astra

QUOTE

  • Read the whole thing (Dan needs a tl;dr or something :-) ): Dan Luu:: Test and verification technique effectiveness with Astra

When we looked at how well agents used test/verification techniques in August1, we saw that GPT-5.6 Sol generally did what you might call a caricature of various techniques when asked to use a technique or library such as TDD, QuickCheck, Lean 4, etc.; not specifying any particular test method (which we’ll call Default) resulted in many worthless unit tests, which was one of the best performing conditions because asking agents to test in specific ways mostly made them worse. In that eval, we gave agents the Zstd RFC and asked them to implement Zstd (with an addendum for how they should test for all conditions other than Default).

QUOTE:

so openssh on musl linux (alpine, openwrt, buildroot, yocto, and a lot of the docker images you’ve pulled) has had a little problem since 2016.

accounts that should never take a password at all (root, your key-only deploy user, ldap users, the default user on alpine’s aws and azure images) take any password longer than 256 characters.

item.title: Adële's blog:: Small, simple with no CSS tricks 'dumb' graphical mastodon client Home Timeline - SmolFedi/smolfedi.pollux.casa
item.description:
Discovered: Nov 12, 2026 04:10 (UTC) Adële’s blog:: Small, simple with no CSS tricks ‘dumb’ graphical mastodon client Home Timeline - SmolFedi/smolfedi.pollux.casa

  • The Fediverse deserves a dumb graphical client ¦ Adële’s blog

QUOTE:

What I wanted was something in between: a client that runs in a plain browser, handles images properly, but does not require a JavaScript engine to display a list of posts. The API returns JSON; a server-side script can turn that JSON into HTML just fine. We have been doing that for 25 years.

So I built SmolFedi.

It is a PHP application. No npm, no Composer, no build step. It uses a SQLite database and basic PHP sessions. Every page is generated server-side and sent as plain HTML. It supports multiple accounts, timelines, notifications, polls, media attachments with alt text, content warnings, compose, reply, boost, favourite, everything I actually use day to day. CSS stays within smolweb Grade B. There is not a single line of JavaScript in the codebase.

It works with Mastodon, GoToSocial and certainly other compatible Fediverse platforms. It works in Firefox, in Chromium, in Safari, in any browser that can render HTML and display a JPEG such as Dillo or Netsurf.

I am not claiming this is the right client for everyone. If you want a smooth single-page experience with live updates and animations, SmolFedi is not that. But if you want to browse the Fediverse on a modest device, a slow connection, or simply a setup where you would rather not run megabytes of JavaScript fetched from the web, SmolFedi is for you.

The source is on Codeberg and a demo instance on Pollux
